content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To have a bonfire, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Stack the medium-sized logs in a teepee formation (10 minutes)
Step 2. Clear dry leaves from the perimeter (20 minutes)
Step 3. Check the local wind speed and direction (5 minutes)
Step 4. Light the kindling with a long-reach lighter (2 minutes)
Step 5. Position the heavy oak stumps at the base (15 minutes)
Step 6. Dig a shallow fire pit in the dirt (30 minutes)
Step 7. Select a safe, flat location away from low-hanging branches (15 minutes)
Step 8. Fill a backup water bucket for emergencies (5 minutes)
Step 9. Gather dry twigs and small branches (20 minutes)
Step 10. Invite the neighbors over for the evening (10 minutes)
Step 11. Bring out the folding lawn chairs (10 minutes)
Step 12. Check the woodpile for dampness (5 minutes)
Step 13. Arrange the seating in a wide circle (10 minutes)
Step 14. Skewer the marshmallows on sticks (10 minutes)
Step 15. Crumple up old newspaper for tinder (5 minutes)
Step 16. Place tinder in the center of the pit (5 minutes)
Step 17. Locate the fire poker in the garage (5 minutes)
Step 18. Set aside a pile of "quick-burn" pine (15 minutes)
Step 19. Buy a bag of artisan firewood (30 minutes)
Step 20. Clean the metal roasting skewers (10 minutes)
Step 21. Place the largest logs on top of the structure (15 minutes)
Step 22. Lean the fire poker against a nearby chair (2 minutes)
Step 23. Carry the heavy logs from the shed to the pit (20 minutes)
Step 24. Sort the gathered wood by thickness (15 minutes)
Step 25. Check the 24-hour weather forecast (5 minutes)
Step 26. Rake the surrounding grass to remove debris (20 minutes)
Step 27. Create a ring of decorative stones around the pit (40 minutes)
Step 28. Set up a small side table for snacks (10 minutes)
Step 29. Shake out the outdoor blankets (5 minutes)
Step 30. Confirm the burn permit regulations online (10 minutes)
Step 31. Put on a durable outdoor jacket (5 minutes)
Step 32. Sweep the patio area (15 minutes)
Step 33. Open the package of graham crackers (2 minutes)
Step 34. Adjust the log spacing for better airflow (5 minutes)
Step 35. Lay down a base layer of sand in the pit (20 minutes)
Step 36. Prepare the chocolate bars for s'mores (5 minutes)
Step 37. Check the fuel level in the lighter (2 minutes)
Step 38. Fetch the shovel from the tool shed (5 minutes)
Step 39. Sprinkle a handful of dry pine needles over the tinder (5 minutes)
Step 40. Put on heat-resistant work gloves (2 minutes)
Step 41. Prop the heavy logs against the teepee (10 minutes)
Step 42. Clear a path from the house to the fire area (25 minutes)
Step 43. Drape blankets over the back of the chairs (10 minutes)
Step 44. Place large boundary stones to mark the safety zone (30 minutes)
Step 45. Check the flashlight batteries (3 minutes)
Step 46. Mark the fire diameter with a stick (5 minutes)
Step 47. Organize the s'mores ingredients on a tray (10 minutes)
Step 48. Snap long branches into smaller pieces (15 minutes)
Step 49. Inspect the garden hose for leaks (10 minutes)
Step 50. Ensure the fire extinguisher is pressurized (5 minutes)
Step 51. Arrange the medium logs for optimal drafting (10 minutes)
Step 52. Double-check the distance from the house (5 minutes)
Step 53. Stack the reserved firewood nearby (15 minutes)
Step 54. Layer the smallest twigs over the paper (10 minutes)
Step 55. Retrieve the bonfire kit from storage (15 minutes)
Step 56. Unroll the garden hose to the fire site (10 minutes)
Step 57. Set up the outdoor Bluetooth speaker (5 minutes)
Step 58. Create a small "chimney" gap in the wood stack (5 minutes)
Step 59. Place the "starter" sticks in the gap (5 minutes)
Step 60. Select a upbeat playlist for the gathering (5 minutes)
Step 61. Move the propane grill away from the fire zone (10 minutes)
Step 62. Take a final look at the fire structure (2 minutes)
Step 63. Strip the bark off the roasting sticks (20 minutes)
Step 64. Check the outdoor faucet pressure (5 minutes)
Step 65. Set up the citronella candles (15 minutes)
Step 66. Borrow extra firewood from a neighbor (30 minutes)
Step 67. Clean the ash from the previous fire (15 minutes)
Step 68. Bring out the cooler of drinks (10 minutes)
Step 69. Test the hose spray nozzle (2 minutes)
Step 70. Put on safety glasses for the initial lighting (2 minutes)
